title: sampled-span-annotations-and-epoch-timer-harness-for-scheduler-hotpath
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need lower-overhead, higher-signal instrumentation for the scheduler hotpath and KV cache eviction/lookup code so microbenchmarks and real-world traffic can be correlated without perturbing latency distributions. This PR adds sampled span annotations and lightweight epoch timers around key scheduler states (enqueue, batch-assembly, kernel-dispatch, kv-lookup, kv-apply) and a small microbenchmark harness that emits deterministic workloads to exercise batching and eviction behavior. Changes: 1) lightweight sampled-span API (runtime/trace/sample_span.h + C/TS bindings) with configurable sampling rate per-route; 2) epoch timers (runtime/trace/epoch_timer.{cc,h}) with sub-microsecond counters and wall/CPU time; 3) scheduler probes inserted at hotpoints with taggable annotations for model_id, seq_len_bucket, and batch_size; 4) a microbench harness (tools/perf/scheduler_epoch_bench) that runs synthetic arrival patterns and produces JSON summaries compatible with our perf-dashboard ingestion; 5) dashboards: added a new dashboard (Perf -> Scheduler Timeline) and a companion CI job to run the microbench on PRs; 6) tests: unit tests for timer math and an integration test that verifies sampled annotation metadata survives through the batching pipeline. Benchmark summary: on a 8-GPU staging cluster with sampling set to 1/50, observed 8-12% reduction in the noise of p50/p95 latency estimates across 10 runs (p95 stdev reduced from 22ms to 6ms) and identified a 7% tail amplification when kv cache miss rate > 15% at small batch sizes. Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default (trace.sampled.enabled=false); enable for internal perf jobs and canary for 10% of incoming requests. Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing tracing exporters; sampled annotations are additive. review_conversation: Diego: Can we make sampling rate pluggable per-route? (reply) Maya: yes, config added and documented; default is global but route override is supported
Priya: Please ensure timers don't allocate in the hotpath. (reply) Maya: epoch_timer uses thread-local preallocated buffers and only records scalar writes; added a micro-optimisation after review
Liam: observed flakiness on CI perf job initially. (reply) Maya: fixed harness timing jitter by pinning CPU affinity in the bench binary; re-ran job as part of CI
release_notes: Added sampled span annotation and epoch timers for scheduler hotpath with a microbenchmark harness and dashboard. Default off behind feature flag. Improves observability of batching and KV-cache interactions; helps reduce noise in latency experiments.
